author: s-morgan-jeffries
body:
## Summary

- The IMAP auth decision in #70 covered config-level fallback (no Keychain entry → AppleScript) but left runtime failures (offline, revoked creds, timeouts, protocol errors) unspecified.
- This PR adds seven explicit invariants to `docs/research/imap-auth-options-decision.md` under a new "Graceful degradation invariants" section, and updates the delegation code sketch in `imap-hybrid-approach.md` to match.
- **Core principle:** every MCP tool must function when IMAP is not available for any reason. AppleScript + Mail.app is the universal baseline; IMAP is always an additive enhancement. A user offline against a local LLM still gets working read/search tools.

## Invariants (summary)

1. AppleScript baseline — universal; every tool works without IMAP.
2. Per-account opt-in via Keychain entry presence.
3. Runtime failure → per-operation fallback (catches `OSError`, `socket.timeout`, `LoginError`, `IMAPClientError`, explicit timeout).
4. ≤3s connect timeout so offline fallback is fast.
5. Quiet fallback at DEBUG; first failure per account emits one WARNING.
6. Write ops (send/reply/forward) always AppleScript.
7. No whole-session disable — per-operation fallback only.

Full text in the decision doc. The `imap-hybrid-approach.md` delegation sketch now shows the try/except pattern and connect-timeout constant, so readers can't miss the runtime-fallback requirement.

## Why now

#41 is the next keystone issue — design of `imap_connector.py` + `keychain.py`. Without these invariants locked in the decision doc, #41 could reasonably produce a version that raises network errors to the MCP caller instead of silently degrading. Post-merge, #41 gets a comment with acceptance criteria derived from these invariants so the principle travels with the implementation.

## Test plan

- [x] `make lint` — passes (no code changes; docs only).
- [x] `make test` — 306 passed (ran via pre-push hook).
- [ ] Reviewer reads the new "Graceful degradation invariants" section in `imap-auth-options-decision.md` and confirms the seven invariants capture the intent.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the updated delegation code sketch in `imap-hybrid-approach.md` reads as "must catch these exceptions" rather than "might catch these exceptions."

## Post-merge action (user-gated)

After merge, I will — pending your go-ahead — add a comment to #41 with explicit acceptance criteria:

- Delegation layer catches `OSError`, `socket.timeout`, `LoginError`, `IMAPClientError` at every IMAP call site.
- IMAP connect timeout ≤3s.
- First failure per account per process emits WARNING; subsequent DEBUG.
- Unit tests cover: missing Keychain entry, connect-refused, connect-timeout, LoginError, in-session IMAPClientError.
- Integration test covers fallback-when-offline.
- Write ops remain AppleScript-only.

No changes to `src/` or tests in this PR. Production behavior unchanged (no IMAP production code yet).

### Motivation
- Normalise CRM endpoints by removing the redundant `general` segment so utilities target `/crm` (and public `/api/v1/crm`) instead of `/crm/general` to match the internal API shape. 
- Avoid cache collisions and stale entries during the endpoint rename by migrating and invalidating both new and legacy cache keys.

body:
## Ticket number

PDJB-780

## Goal of change

Replace the single shared feature-flag config across test, nft, and prod with separate per-environment configs so each environment can be tuned independently.

## Description of main change(s)

- Adds `application-test.yml` and `application-nft.yml` under `src/main/resources/`, each containing the complete `features.feature-flags` list. Spring picks these up via `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE = "default, <env_name>"` already set by terraform — until now the env-specific profile was a no-op.
- Updates `application.yml` so the default profile represents production: `failover-test-endpoints` is now `false` (was `true`) and the PDJB-780 TODO comment above `subject-identifier-page` has been removed.
- Extends `FeatureFlagConsistencyTests` with nested `TestProfileTests` and `NftProfileTests` mirroring the existing `LocalProfileTests` / `IntegrationProfileTests` pattern, so a missing flag in either new env file is caught at CI rather than at environment boot.

Final flag matrix:

| Flag | Default (prod) | test | nft |
|---|---|---|---|
| failover-test-endpoints | false | true | true |
| joint-landlords | false | false | false |
| subject-identifier-page | true | true | true |

## Anything you'd like to highlight to the reviewer?

- `subject-identifier-page` is intentionally `true` in all three environments for now. The deleted TODO suggested it should only be enabled in test, but the team's current preference is to leave it on everywhere and disable per environment later. Flagging because the deleted comment line might invite a question.
- Production behaviour change: `failover-test-endpoints` flips from `true` to `false` on the next prod deploy. This is intentional — failover test endpoints should not be live in prod.
- Local bootRun smoke test was skipped because the new `TestProfileTests` / `NftProfileTests` boot a Spring context with the same profiles and exercise the same `FeatureFlagConfig.afterPropertiesSet()` validation that fires at env startup. No other config varies by `test` / `nft` profile in this PR.
- The full gradle `test` suite was not run locally; only `uk.gov.communities.prsdb.webapp.config.featureFlags.*` was run because changes are isolated to feature-flag YAML and the targeted classes cover the consistency invariants. CI will run the full suite.

- [x] Unit tests for new logic (e.g. new service methods) have been added
- [x] TODO comments referencing this JIRA ticket have been searched for and removed

body:
## Summary

New reusable thin-strip banner DS primitive for inline warning/info/danger/success messages. Plus a prototype wiring that surfaces a banner at the top of the grading desk's manuscript area when the active student has one or more review flags.

Matches the user's mockup: thin horizontal strip, colored icon, inline message, rounded border — sitting above the manuscript page.

## New DS primitive — `src/components/ui/banner.tsx`

```tsx
<Banner variant="warning">
  Review carefully — grades aren't usually this high for Rohan Verma.
</Banner>
```

**API**
- `variant`: `'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'` (default `'info'`)
- `icon`: optional ReactNode override (defaults to variant-specific lucide: `Info` / `CheckCircle2` / `AlertTriangle` / `XCircle`)
- `onDismiss`: if provided, renders a right-aligned × button
- `children`: message content

**Styling** — entirely via `--status-{info,success,warning,error}(-bg)` tokens. No hardcoded colors. Light/dark themes adapt automatically.

**Accessibility** — role is `alert` for warning/danger variants, `status` for info/success.

## Type additions — `src/lib/store/grading-store.ts`

Exported types + optional field:

```ts
export type ReviewFlagSeverity = 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
export interface ReviewFlag {
  severity: ReviewFlagSeverity
  message: string
  criterionId?: string  // for future per-criterion banners
}
// on StudentSubmission:
reviewFlags?: ReviewFlag[]
```

Seeded on 5 store students for forward compatibility:

| Student | Assignment | Variant |
|---|---|---|
| Rohan Verma | se-101 | warning |
| Arjun Mehta | dbms-202 | info |
| Priya Sharma | ds-303 | danger |
| Arjun Sharma | AI-ETH-01 | warning |
| Priya Iyer | AI-ETH-01 | success |

## Grading desk render — `src/app/dashboard/evaluation/[id]/page.tsx`

The evaluation/[id] page uses its own inline 60-student mock (`allSubmissions`), not the store students. Extended that mock to carry `reviewFlags` and seeded 5 discoverable indices — one per variant:

- i = 0 → warning (grade anomaly)
- i = 4 → info (low OCR)
- i = 7 → danger (late submission)
- i = 13 → warning (grade trend)
- i = 19 → success (consistent performer)

Render block sits between the text-selection-mode strip and the manuscript `ScrollArea`, mapping over `currentStudent.reviewFlags`. Students without flags render exactly as before — no layout shift.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- Per-criterion banners on rubric rows — `criterionId` field is present in the type but unused for now
- Persisting flags to a backend (in-memory prototype only)
- Wiring `onDismiss` into the grading desk (prop exists on `Banner` but not passed — flags stay visible while viewing)

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/components/ui/banner.tsx` | NEW |
| `src/lib/store/grading-store.ts` | Type + optional field + 5 seed flags |
| `src/app/dashboard/evaluation/[id]/page.tsx` | Import + render block + local mock extension |

- [ ] `/dashboard/evaluation/se-101` — open. Click the first student in the triage sidebar (index 0). Amber warning banner appears above the manuscript: *"Review carefully — grades aren't usually this high for …"*
- [ ] Click the 5th student (index 4) — blue info banner (OCR warning)

- [ ] Dark mode toggle (if theme switcher available) — banner colors adapt via `--status-*` dark overrides

author: seven332
body:
## Summary

- In `--print` mode Claude Code emits its final `type=result` event and then waits for its own backgrounded Bash tasks to drain — a runaway task can hold the CLI (and the sandbox) alive for tens of minutes past the user-visible answer, until external Ably cancel tears things down (see #10879 for the 28-minute run we traced).
- `guest-agent/src/cli.rs` now drives a `ReapState` FSM on the CLI's process group when `type=result` is observed: `Idle → SigtermPending → SigkillPending → Done`. `child.wait()` fires within seconds of end_turn and the rest of `execute()` runs as intended.
- `guest-mock-claude` gains a `@hang-after-result` test prefix; `guest-agent/tests/post_result_reap.rs` spawns the real mock binary and asserts the FSM reaps it within the configured grace window.

## How it works

| From             | Trigger        | To              | Action |
|------------------|----------------|-----------------|--------|
| `Idle`           | `type=result`  | `SigtermPending`| arm sigterm grace |
| `SigtermPending` | deadline fires | `SigkillPending`| `SIGTERM pgid`, arm sigkill grace |
| `SigkillPending` | deadline fires | `Done`          | `SIGKILL pgid` |
| _any pending_    | `child.wait()` | `Done`          | (no signal — CLI exited on its own) |

One pinned `Sleep` serves both phases via `reset()`; the single eligibility guard is `reap_state.is_pending() && cli_status.is_none()`. `Done` is sticky so a late second `type=result` can't re-arm.

`SIGTERM -pgid` covers grandchild processes too (the runaway `xargs` pipeline is a bash-spawned grandchild of the CLI). The same `libc::kill(-pgid, ...)` pattern is already used by the stuck-tool watchdog and the heartbeat-failure path.

## Configuration

| Constant | Default | Env override |
|---|---|---|
| `POST_RESULT_SIGTERM_GRACE_SECS` | 10 | `VM0_POST_RESULT_SIGTERM_GRACE_SECS` |
| `POST_RESULT_SIGKILL_GRACE_SECS` | 5  | `VM0_POST_RESULT_SIGKILL_GRACE_SECS` |

Also factored env.rs's numeric env-override parsing into `u64_env_or(name, default)` so the existing `STUCK_TOOL_TIMEOUT` and the two new grace knobs share one bit of logic instead of three match statements.

## Scope correction

Stdin is already `Stdio::null()` (`cli.rs:124`), so "close stdin to let the CLI see EOF" — which I'd originally suggested in #10879 — is a no-op. The CLI isn't waiting on stdin; it's blocked on its own backgrounded-task drain. Signalling the process group is the right lever.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build -p guest-agent` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p guest-agent -p guest-mock-claude --all-targets --no-deps` clean (incl. `-D clippy::unreachable` / `-D clippy::unwrap_used` / `-D clippy::expect_used`)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [x] **New** `cargo test -p guest-agent --test post_result_reap` — e2e FSM test spawns real mock, converges in ~1s (vs mock's 3600s hang) with signal-based exit code
- [x] `cargo test -p guest-agent` — 80 unit + 33 integration + 1 e2e reap pass (two new unit tests cover `ReapState::is_pending` and the arming guard)
- [x] `cargo test -p guest-mock-claude` — 19 pass

Closes #10879.

## One-Line Summary
Audit records from CLI query execution now show up promptly in the web audit feed instead of waiting for a later read to build the projection.

## User-Facing Changes
- Running `onequery query exec` or `onequery query validate` now primes the audit feed projection after the workflow completes.
- The audit page fetches fresh data when opened, polls the newest page while projection lag exists, and keeps a low-frequency heartbeat for CLI activity from outside the browser.
- The audit filters include an explicit refresh icon button, and projection-lag copy now says the page will refresh while the feed catches up.

## Why This Changed
The audit event log was the source of truth, but the web feed read from a derived projection that was only synchronized lazily during authenticated audit API reads. A successful CLI command could persist audit workflow events while the browser still showed cached empty feed data until a later refresh or query caused projection catch-up.

## How It Changed
- CLI query execute and validate workflows now call `syncCliQueryAuditFeedProjection` after workflow completion.
- Projection sync failure is non-fatal because the feed projection is derived state; the boundary uses `Result.tryPromise` and a typed `TaggedError` so failure context is preserved in logs.
- The audit route loader uses `fetchQuery` instead of `ensureQueryData` so opening the route does not reuse stale empty data.
- Audit list query options set `staleTime: 0`, always refetch on mount/reconnect/window focus, and use functional polling: 1s while projection lag exists, 5s for the newest caught-up page, and no polling for cursor pages.

## Bug Fixes
- Under CLI activity outside the browser, audit rows could be persisted but missing from `/audit` until a later authenticated read synchronized the projection; the CLI now advances the projection immediately after query workflows.
- Under cached empty audit query data, opening the audit route could avoid the API read that would catch projection up; the route now blocks on a fresh fetch.

## Extra Context / Decisions (Optional)
The durable source of truth remains the audit workflow/event tables. This PR only advances the derived feed projection earlier and makes the UI freshness contract explicit; a later outbox/projector plus SSE or websocket invalidation could replace the 5s heartbeat.

author: srfwb
body:
## Summary

Polish pass on every modal in the app plus two transactional guarantees on project operations.

All five modals (Create, Rename, Delete, Confirm, Prompt) advertise `aria-modal="true"` to screen readers but did not honor the contract: no Escape, no focus trap, no return of focus to the trigger on close. A new `useModalA11y` hook centralises that plumbing; every modal adopts it. `aria-labelledby` now points at the title so the dialog is announced properly.

`createProject` was not atomic: if any template write failed mid-way (antivirus lock, quota, OneDrive), the user ended up with an orphan folder on disk and no project in the index — every subsequent `Create` at the same path hit "dossier existe déjà" with no way out. Failures now roll back the partial directory before bubbling up.

`deleteProject` had the mirror problem: `fs_delete_dir` ran after the VFS and watcher teardown, so a disk failure left the store in a half-torn-down state. The disk delete now happens first; on failure nothing else changes, and the operation can be retried safely thanks to the A1 idempotency tweak to `fs_delete_dir`.

`PromptModal` (create/rename file from the FileTree) exposed raw Rust error strings (`"invalid path segment '.'"`) in a French, pedagogical UI. A new `localizeFileError` helper maps the common backend errors to friendly French messages. The modal also validates the name inline: the submit button disables when the value is empty, contains forbidden characters, or (in rename mode) contains a slash.

`RenameProjectModal` grew a `submitting` state to avoid double-submit once an async backend is wired in (matches `CreateProjectModal` / `DeleteProjectDialog`).

## What changed

### User-facing

- Escape closes every modal. Tab cycles inside the modal instead of escaping to the page underneath. Clicking the backdrop closes the modal (except while an operation is in flight). Focus returns to whatever element had it before the modal opened.
- Failed project creation leaves the disk clean; the same name can be retried immediately.
- Failed "delete with disk removal" keeps the project in the list and shows the raw error — no more orphan state where the project disappears but the folder survives.
- Creating or renaming a file with `.`, `..`, `/`, or a forbidden character is caught at the input level with a French hint rather than after submission as a raw English error.

### Internal

- New `src/hooks/useModalA11y.ts` — generic hook over `HTMLElement`, takes a container ref + `onClose`, handles Escape, focus trap, return of focus, and optional `initialFocus`.
- New `src/ide/shell/fileErrorMessages.ts` with `localizeFileError(unknown) -> string`. Six test cases cover the main translation paths plus the fallback.
- `CreateProjectModal`, `RenameProjectModal`, `DeleteProjectDialog`, `ConfirmDialog`, `PromptModal` (inside `FileTree`) all consume the hook. ARIA `aria-labelledby` wired to a `id` on the title.
- `actions.createProjectImpl` wraps the template write loop in try/catch and calls `fs_delete_dir` on the partial path before rethrowing.
- `actions.deleteProjectImpl` reorders so `fs_delete_dir` runs before the VFS/watcher teardown.
- `FileTree.PromptModal` adds `allowSlash` prop (true for create, false for rename), inline validation, disabled submit on invalid input, and routes thrown errors through `localizeFileError`.

body:
## Summary

Wires a full OAuth 2.1 flow on `mcp.winlab.tw` with Keycloak as the actual IdP (federated via Supabase OIDC), then adds 9 real MCP tools on top of it. Pattern lifted from [`Office-of-AI-Affairs/mcp.ai.winlab.tw`](https://github.com/Office-of-AI-Affairs/mcp.ai.winlab.tw) — no custom JWT signing, we just pipe Supabase's own access token through as the OAuth access token.

## Flow

```
MCP client → /mcp (401 + WWW-Authenticate)
  → /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
  → /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
  → POST /oauth/register → client_id
  → GET /oauth/authorize?client_id=...&code_challenge=... → "Continue with Keycloak"
  → supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({ provider: 'keycloak', redirectTo: /oauth/callback?mcp_* })
  → Keycloak login → Supabase → /oauth/callback
  → exchangeCodeForSession → mint MCP code bundling Supabase tokens → redirect to client's redirect_uri
  → POST /oauth/token (code + code_verifier) → PKCE check → access_token + refresh_token
  → POST /mcp (Bearer <access_token>) → tools run under user's RLS
```

## Commits (8)

1. **DB migration** — `mcp_oauth_clients` + `mcp_oauth_auth_codes` + SECURITY DEFINER RPCs
2. **SDK swap** — `mcp-handler` → `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` direct, add supabase helpers
3. **OAuth lib + discovery + register** — `lib/auth/*` + `.well-known/*` + `/oauth/register`
4. **Authorize page** — "Continue with Keycloak" button, MCP params piggyback on `redirectTo`
5. **Callback + token** — `/oauth/callback` mints MCP code from Supabase session; `/oauth/token` handles `authorization_code` + `refresh_token`
6. **Gate /mcp** — bearer check + `supabase.auth.getUser()` + user-aware `ping`
7. **Bento tools (5)** — `list_restaurants`, `list_active_orders`, `get_order`, `add_order_item`, `remove_my_order_item`
8. **Leave tools (4)** — `list_recent`, `list_mine`, `request`, `cancel_mine`

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck --filter=mcp`
- [x] `bun run build --filter=mcp` — all 9 routes emitted
- [x] `bun run lint --filter=mcp`
- [x] **Local dev smoke tests** against `http://localhost:3001`:
  - [x] `/` 200
  - [x] `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` serves full metadata with S256
  - [x] `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` points at `/mcp` + AS
  - [x] `POST /mcp` unauthenticated → 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...`
  - [x] `GET /oauth/authorize` with bad params → Zod-rendered error page
  - [x] `GET /oauth/authorize` with unknown client_id → "Unknown client_id"
  - [x] DB migration applied via Supabase MCP

  - [x] `GET /oauth/authorize` with real client → renders "Continue with Keycloak"
- [ ] End-to-end Keycloak click-through (blocked on Dashboard config, see below)
- [ ] MCP Inspector smoke test with real `ping` tool call once end-to-end works

## Dashboard steps before this is useful

1. **Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs** — add:
   - `http://localhost:3001/oauth/callback`
   - `https://mcp.winlab.tw/oauth/callback`

## Summary

Downgrades the PyTorch base image for both NCCL preflight containers from `26.03-py3` (CUDA 13.2) to `25.03-py3` (CUDA 12.8.1).

## Problem

Crusoe clusters run driver `570.133.20` which supports up to CUDA 12.8. The NCCL test binaries compiled against CUDA 13.2 fail on every Crusoe node with:

```
CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
```

VP and GCP clusters work because they run driver `580.126.09` (CUDA 13.0+).

CUDA forward compatibility (`cuda-compat`) does NOT bridge 570 → 13.x — the package is explicitly listed as incompatible.

## Fix

Use PyTorch `25.03-py3` (CUDA 12.8.1) which works on both driver 570+ and 580+. The NCCL loopback and allreduce tests measure NVLink/IB hardware bandwidth — they don't use CUDA 13 features.

- [ ] Verify loopback still passes on VP (driver 580)

author: revdan
body:
## Summary

First of two coordinated breaking releases on the road to v1.0.0. Two commits:

**1. Remove `operator_ref` end-to-end.** The optional operator-supplied sidecar on `Entry` was a privacy smell — plain-text operator strings in the OSS schema with only byte-length and control-char validation. Since the field was effectively write-only at the API surface (no GET path exposed it), dropping it has no capability cost for callers who were using it properly. Column drop, Ash attribute removed, validation module deleted, accept list trimmed. The canonical `entry_hash` bytes are unchanged — it was already shape-invariant to `operator_ref` — so the v0.15.0 frozen vectors replay green against this code (zero-drift proof).

**2. Add entry UUID capture.** With `operator_ref` gone, operators still need to learn the wallop-assigned UUIDs of the entries they just submitted so they can maintain a `(uuid ↔ their-own-id)` mapping locally (encrypted at rest). Two mechanisms:

- `PATCH /api/v1/draws/:id/entries` now returns `meta.inserted_entries: [{uuid}]` in **submission order** — per-batch, zero round-trip. Transaction-atomic; partial batch failure rolls back.
- New authenticated `GET /api/v1/draws/:id/entries` — api_key-scoped, keyset-paginated (`?after=<uuid>&limit=<n>`), sorted UUID-ascending, works at any draw status including `:open`. At `:locked` the response is byte-identical to the public `/proof/:id/entries`. Used for post-TTL recovery after a dropped response and as the canonical UUID-sorted source for downstream manifest Merkle construction.

### Submission-order correctness

The server pre-generates entry UUIDs in Elixir via `Ash.UUID.generate/0` (which uses `:crypto.strong_rand_bytes/1` under the hood — still server-side entropy, no operator influence) and passes them as explicit inputs to the bulk insert. Correlation is tautological, not order-dependent on a bulk-create contract Ash does not guarantee.

### Operator-supplied UUIDs are NOT accepted

The `Entry` `:create` policy is still `forbid_if(always())` for external callers. Only the internal `AddEntries` change module, called with `authorize?: false` from the `add_entries` action, can pass a pre-generated UUID in. A low-entropy operator-chosen UUID would reintroduce the brute-force surface the v0.15.0 UUID refactor killed.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `AddEntries` order-preservation metadata (5-entry submission, UUIDs match submitted weight positions)
- [x] Controller tests for `:create` (meta.inserted_entries shape, submission order, ownership, invalid payloads, cross-operator 404)
- [x] Controller tests for `:index` (UUID-ascending sort, keyset pagination, cross-operator 404, any status)
- [x] Existing frozen vectors (`spec/vectors/entry-hash.json`) replay green against the new code — byte-level proof the canonical form did not change
- [x] Full suite: 372 core + 153 web = 525 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `mix format` clean
- [x] `mix credo --strict` clean

## Migration

One breaking change: `entries[*].ref` on `add_entries` payloads no longer accepted. Callers should drop the field from their request bodies. Migration drops `entries.operator_ref` column.

Response shape change on the happy path: `meta.inserted_entries` is new. Existing parsers that only read `data` will continue to work.

### Motivation

- Autopilot and hunters were performing shallow, single‑vector passes and not exhaustively exploring bypasses, encodings, auth variants, or combinations. The change enforces deeper, systematic coverage to reduce missed techniques.  
- `tools/brain.py` was brittle when autopilot wrote orchestration metadata and used fragile frontmatter updates, causing failures and loss of coverage bookkeeping.  
- The Codex installer used `tomllib` parsing that breaks on Python 3.10 environments, causing CI/test failures; this needed to be tolerant of older stdlib availability.

### Description

- Added a mandatory "Depth Engine" to the autopilot skill that requires a per-endpoint `variant matrix`, baseline controls, a minimum-attempt floor, combination tests, structural delta capture, and brain coverage ledger persistence (`.claude/skills/autopilot/SKILL.md`).  
- Added an `Exhaustive Depth Protocol` to the `/hunt` skill so manual and semi-autonomous hunts follow the same matrix discipline and must write explicit exhaustion reasons (`.claude/skills/hunt/SKILL.md`).  
- Expanded `tools/brain.py` `record_result` to accept orchestration metadata statuses used by skills (`recon`, `waf-map`, `waf-bypass`, `browser-rejected`, `da-killed`, `chain`, `duplicate`, `policy`, etc.), to write into appropriate technique files, and to append readable notes into target files.  
- Replaced brittle frontmatter replacement with a regex-based helper `_touch_last_updated` to reliably refresh `last_updated` in target files.  
- Removed a hard `tomllib` dependency in `tools/installer/targets/codex.py` so the installer does not fail on Python 3.10 where `tomllib` may not be present.  
- Added unit tests (`tests/test_brain.py`) that exercise the new `brain.record_result` statuses and verify `last_updated` is refreshed correctly.  
- Minor wiring: autopilot/hunt SKILLs now instruct hunter agents to include the variant matrix and minimum attempt constraints and to record coverage via `python3 tools/brain.py record <target> recon "coverage-<class>" "<coverage>"`.

### Testing

- Ran the added unit file `tests/test_brain.py`; it passed (`2 passed`).

## Summary
- recover the active macOS chat when the SSE stream reconnects without a full gateway reconnect
- broaden SSE `Accept` headers to allow JSON error responses during stream setup
- add SSE handshake diagnostics so future feedback bundles include HTTP status and response headers for parse failures

## Root Cause
The desktop client only triggered active-conversation history catch-up on `.daemonDidReconnect`. When the SSE stream dropped and reconnected on its own, the sidebar refreshed but the active chat did not, so assistant replies that completed during the gap could appear in web but remain missing in macOS until the user sent another message.

Separately, the SSE transport was logging generic `cannot parse response` failures without enough response metadata to identify whether the upstream returned JSON, a proxy error, or some other non-SSE payload.

## User Impact
- macOS now refetches the active conversation after SSE-only reconnects when a run may have been in flight
- SSE setup is more tolerant of JSON error responses from proxies
- feedback bundles should now show the last SSE handshake status, content type, and proxy-identifying headers when parse failures recur

## Validation
- `swift test --package-path clients --filter "ChatViewModelTests/test(ReconnectDuringStreamingTriggersHistoryCatchUp|EventStreamReconnectDuringStreamingTriggersHistoryCatchUp)"`

## Summary

After a successful train, the UI still shows \"Ready to train!\" instead of flipping to cooldown countdown.

author: lijunzh
body:
## What

Phase 1 of #1022 P1. Unifies the sub-agent tool-execution path with the top-level dispatcher. Four bugs collapse into one root cause and one fix.

| ID | Bug | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| **B6** | Sub-agent mutations don't invalidate `SubAgentCache` | Sub-agent loop called `tools.execute()` directly, skipping the `is_mutating_tool` check that lives in `execute_one_tool`. |
| **B7** | Nested `InvokeAgent` from inside a sub-agent silently no-ops | Same skip — fell through to the registry stub: `"InvokeAgent is handled by the inference loop."` with `success=false`. |
| **B8** | `AskUser` from a sub-agent returns a stub error | Same skip — same kind of stub. Sub-agents have a detached `cmd_rx`; routing AskUser there cannot work. |
| **B14** | Pre-flight validation only ran in sequential dispatch | `execute_tools_parallel` and split-batch's parallel arm skipped `validate_tool_call`. Same gap in the sub-agent loop. |

## Fix

**`koda-core/src/sub_agent_dispatch.rs`**
- Filter `AskUser` from every sub-agent's `tool_defs` (B8). Both fg and bg. Joins the existing `fork children cannot spawn sub-agents` filter.
- Pre-flight `validate_tool_call` before the approval check (B14).
- Replace both `tools.execute()` call sites with `execute_one_tool` (B6 + B7).

**`koda-core/src/tool_dispatch.rs`**
- `Box::pin` the recursive `execute_sub_agent` call inside `execute_one_tool`. Mutually-recursive `async fn`s produce an infinitely-sized future (E0733).
- New `validate_then_execute_one_tool` helper. Used by `execute_tools_parallel` and the parallel arm of `execute_tools_split_batch` (B14). Sequential keeps its own validate-then-approve order so the user is never prompted for a tool guaranteed to fail.

**`Design.md`**
- Two new sub-agent invariants: **Single tool-dispatch path**, **Pre-flight validation everywhere**, **No user interaction from sub-agents**.
- `Result caching` invariant updated to note sub-agent dispatch now honors mutation invalidation.

## Why no user interaction from sub-agents

Filter `AskUser` for both fg and bg sub-agents. Discussed offline — sub-agents are *autonomous delegation*. The parent gathers any required input *before* dispatching, then passes the answer in the prompt. This matches Codex / Claude Code / Gemini-CLI's design and avoids two real failure modes:

1. **Multi-sub-agent attribution** — parallel sub-agents racing for the user's attention with no clear "who is asking?" UI.
2. **Bg-agent deadlock** — bg agents have no live `cmd_rx` reachable from the user; an AskUser would hang until cancel.

Cost of being wrong is low (one-PR plumbing change to add fg-only support if a real use case appears). Cost of allowing it now and discovering the attribution problem in production is high.

## Tests

- All 1015 lib tests pass.
- All 20 integration test binaries pass (4 e2e_agent + 7 e2e + sandbox + skills + tools + safety + recovery + ...).
- Clippy clean across `koda-core --features test-support --tests`.
- Workspace builds clean.

A direct nested-invocation regression test was attempted but the env-var `MockProvider` design (each sub-agent instance re-reads `KODA_MOCK_RESPONSES` independently) doesn't support multi-level scenarios cleanly. Filed as a follow-up consideration; the fix here is mechanically obvious from the diff and the build itself enforces it (`Box::pin` is required for E0733, the call sites are line-for-line replacements).

## Context

`check_client_api_key` hits `/v1/metadata` and `/v1/api_tokens/self` on every invocation. When a caller runs bursty scans — notably the GitGuardian VSCode extension, which rescans on every save — this is two API round-trips per scan even though the key state rarely changes between them.

## What has been done

This PR caches a successful auth check on disk for a short TTL (300s) keyed on `(instance_url, api_key_hash)`. While the entry is fresh, `check_client_api_key` returns without contacting the API, provided the cached scopes cover the required ones. A cache entry seeded without scopes (e.g. from `auth login`) still skips `/v1/metadata` but falls through to `/v1/api_tokens/self` when the caller needs scopes.

Trade-off: a server-side key revocation may not be observed for up to the TTL. This is self-healing — the next API call returns 401, which runs through `handle_api_error` and invalidates the cache.

## Validation

- create a test file to scan `echo "my secret" > /tmp/scan-me.txt`
- run `uv run ggshield --debug secret scan path /tmp/scan-me.txt` twice in succession and confirm the second invocation does not log the metadata/api_tokens round-trips

## Summary
Enhanced the AR experience across all pages with interactive fireworks animations, sound effects, and improved visual feedback. Users can now tap to launch fireworks with accompanying audio, while the AR view automatically celebrates new artwork discoveries.

## Key Changes

**world.html (3D AR View)**
- Replaced static fireworks with `AnimatedFirework` class featuring launch and burst phases
- Added Web Audio API sound effects: whistle (launch) and boom (explosion)
- Implemented tap-to-launch fireworks on click/touch (only when not panning)
- Auto-launch fireworks every 2-4 seconds (max 5 concurrent)
- Improved animation timing with delta-time based updates
- Updated hint text to indicate tap-to-launch functionality

**index.html (Landing Page)**
- Added animated background with floating fireworks emojis and sparkling particles
- Enhanced visual hierarchy with larger main emoji, gradient text, and drop shadows
- Implemented pulsing subtitle and button animations with shine effects
- Created decorative background elements with CSS animations

**ar.html (Camera AR View)**
- Added 2D particle system for on-screen fireworks bursts
- Integrated Web Audio API for whistle and boom sound effects
- Changed tap behavior from view reset to fireworks launch
- Auto-celebrate new artwork with burst animation at random screen position
- Updated status messages to reflect new tap-to-launch interaction
- Added canvas resize handling for particle effects

## Implementation Details
- Web Audio API uses oscillators for whistle tones and noise buffers for boom effects
- Particle physics includes gravity and air resistance for realistic motion
- Animations use requestAnimationFrame with delta-time for frame-rate independent updates
- Touch and mouse events differentiate between pan gestures and tap interactions
- Fireworks are pooled and removed when animation completes to manage memory
